motifs: Institutional or authoritarian obedience ('Believe! Work! Die!') identified and rejected as a novel's implicit ideological message
Terse, sardonic compression of a critique into a parodic three-word slogan
reading.significance: Brief as it is, this remark is a clear, quotable data point for Dick's lifelong suspicion of narratives that ask their audience to submit to institutional or hierarchical authority without question -- the same suspicion that runs through his fiction's recurring interest in ordinary people who refuse compliance with corrupt or oppressive systems. Its appearance in a secondary profile rather than as a preserved standalone document means the full context of the original letter -- what prompted it, whether Time published it, and what else it may have said -- is not established by the evidence available in this corpus.
reading.closing_note: The line is preserved only as a quotation inside a later piece of Dick scholarship; no primary copy of the original letter to Time has been located in this corpus.
